scope: Private r98 two-substitution SHA-256 implementation review, separate from preceding post-compaction cognitive return.
reasoning: The eight initial compression words are internal Uint32Array elements; direct accesses select the same values before the rounds.

Feed-forward writes retain order 0 through 7 and the same unsigned coercion; each h[i]+word sum is below 2^33 and exactly representable before >>>0. No later update depends on an earlier updated index.
Input type and 64 MiB cap, padding, endian reads, bit-length encoding, message schedule, compression rounds and lowercase output are unchanged.

The explicit per-block temporary v array and state destructuring are removed. No new worker, timer, state owner, retained buffer or asynchronous boundary is introduced. Actual engine allocation/GC savings are not measured by source inspection.

Digest is used by startup/decoded/worker/engine identity consumers. Their validation must remain intact, and generated custody pins must follow the normal build; this review does not admit any bypass.
